correctness.rationale: The irreducible count generator and stationary linear first/second moment equations are explicitly derived; symbolic simplification yields the stated closed rational covariances. A separate full finite-state rational stationary solver verifies all possible first/second moments for a,b=1,2,3. The generator of the part difference yields mean-square collapse; the accelerated averaged-generator polynomial identities give a Hausdorff-determinate beta moment recursion and joint weak convergence for every proportional growing sequence. Finite checks are corroboration, not proof of the asymptotic theorem.

value.rationale: The natural two-community opposing-stubborn-agent model quantifies persistent polarization: all cross/community pairwise correlations are positive, and even a dense balanced network has a fully uniform stationary voting fraction rather than concentration near an average. The infinite-family result supplies exact finite responses and a ratio-dependent distributional universality law. This is a substantive structural and quantitative social-dynamics statement, not a generic beta-distribution observation or routine isolated computation.
